problems.title: Compare logarithms with nearby integers
problems.question: Order I=log₂7, II=log₃10, III=log₂log₂16.
problems.idea: Evaluate III and estimate the other two.

problems.title: Logarithm domains already conflict
problems.question: Count solutions of log₂(6-x-x²)+log₂(x²-9)=2.
problems.idea: Both logarithm arguments must be strictly positive.
formulas: 6-x-x²>0 gives -3<x<2; x²-9>0 gives x<-3 or x>3.
steps: The two conditions have no common input.
There is no need to combine logarithms or solve a polynomial.

problems.title: Change base after rewriting the factors
problems.question: Evaluate (1-log₂6)(1-log₆12).
problems.idea: Write each 1 as a logarithm with the matching base.

problems.title: Range of tangent plus its reciprocal
problems.question: Find the range of y=√(2^(tanx+cotx)).
problems.idea: Set t=tanx, where t is real and nonzero.
steps: For t>0, t+1/t≥2; for t<0 it is ≤-2. Every value in those intervals is attainable.
Since y=2^((t+1/t)/2), map both intervals through the increasing exponential.

problems.title: A negative exponential difference
problems.question: Solve -0.6<0.2^(x+1)-0.2^(x-1).
problems.idea: Factor the common exponential before dividing by a negative number.
problems.note: No printed interval has this exact endpoint. The interval x>1 includes inputs that fail the inequality.

problems.title: Nested cube roots and logarithms
problems.question: Evaluate -log₃(log₃(∛(∛3))).
problems.idea: Turn the roots into powers first.

problems.title: Reflection in the negative diagonal
problems.question: About which line are y=log₂(-x) and y=(1/2)^x symmetric?
problems.idea: Reflect a point (u,2⁻ᵘ) across y=-x.

problems.title: A positive product allows two negative factors
problems.question: Given ab>0, which identities must hold: I log₃(ab)=log₃a+log₃b; II log₃a²=2log₃a; III log₃(ab)-log₃a²=log₃(b/a)?
problems.idea: Test whether each individual logarithm is defined.
steps: I and II can be undefined when both a,b are negative.
In III every argument is positive, and the quotient rule gives log₃(ab/a²)=log₃(b/a).

problems.title: Intersect the logarithm domain and bound
problems.question: Solve log₂(x²-2x)<3.
problems.idea: Since base 2 exceeds 1, compare its argument with 8.

problems.title: Reciprocal change of base
problems.question: Find log_(√3)(⁶√a) if logₐ27=b.
problems.idea: Write both logarithms using natural logs.
steps: The second expression is the reciprocal of the first.

problems.title: Cone area condition fixes its shape
problems.question: A cone’s base area is π times its axial-section area. Find slant height/base diameter.
problems.idea: The axial section is a triangle of base 2r and height h.

problems.title: An exponential-logarithm identity
problems.question: Solve x^(logₓ2)=2.
problems.idea: The identity holds throughout its domain.
steps: Here the only restrictions are x>0 and x≠1.
Every such input makes the left side exactly 2.

problems.title: A square diagonal in an inclined plane
problems.question: A square’s vertices lie on the two base circles of a cylinder, and its plane makes 60° with the base. Find the tangent of a diagonal’s angle to the base.
problems.idea: Two opposite square edges lie in the parallel base planes.
steps: The diagonal’s angle θ satisfies sinθ=(s√3/2)/(s√2)=√6/4.

problems.title: A product of conjugate logarithm arguments
problems.question: Determine the parity of F(x)=log₂(x+√(1+x²)).
problems.idea: The argument at -x is the reciprocal of the argument at x.
steps: Both arguments are positive for every real x.

problems.title: Factor an equation mixing powers and polynomials
problems.question: Find the product of the roots of x²2^x+8=2x²+2^(x+2).
problems.idea: Group the terms with 2^x.

problems.title: A product adds its exponents
problems.question: Solve 2²·2⁴·…·2^(2k)=0.25⁻²⁸ for natural k.
problems.idea: Write both sides as powers of 2.
steps: Only the positive root is natural.

problems.title: Geometric progression of logarithms
problems.question: logₐx,log_bx,log_cx form a geometric progression. Find logₐb-log_bc.
problems.idea: Use the squared-middle-term condition, with x≠1.
steps: Divide by lna·lnb to get lnb/lna=lnc/lnb.
problems.note: If x=1 and a zero progression is permitted, all three given logarithms vanish for arbitrary valid bases, so the requested difference need not be fixed. The source omits this restriction.

problems.title: A projected cylinder chord
problems.question: In a radius-5 cylinder, AB joins its two base circles, makes 45° with the base, and is distance 4 from the axis. Find AB.
problems.idea: Its projection is a chord at distance 4 from the base centre.

problems.title: Largest equilateral triangle in a ball
problems.question: A ball has radius R=2·⁴√3. Find the greatest possible area of an inscribed equilateral triangle.
problems.idea: Its plane-section circle is largest when it is a great circle.
steps: The largest section radius is R, attained by a plane through the centre.

problems.title: Sphere inscribed in a cylinder
problems.question: A sphere is inscribed in a cylinder of volume V. Find the sphere volume.
problems.idea: The cylinder radius is r and its height is 2r.

problems.title: Resolve an oblique segment twice
problems.question: AB lies in one face of a dihedral angle β and makes angle α with its edge. Find the sine of AB’s angle to the other face.
problems.idea: Its perpendicular-to-edge component has length AB sinα.
formulas: Normal distance to the second face=AB sinα sinβ.
steps: Divide that distance by AB, the segment length.

problems.title: Sphere tangent to a right triangle’s sides
problems.question: A right triangle has perimeter 2p,hypotenuse c. All three sides are tangent to a sphere of radius p+c. Find the centre’s distance to the triangle plane.
problems.idea: The plane section tangent to the sides is the triangle’s incircle.

problems.title: Angle between two diagonal cube planes
problems.question: Find the cosine of the acute angle between planes BA₁C₁ and BA₁D₁ in a cube.
problems.idea: Take normals in a unit cube.
steps: Their dot product is 2, and lengths are √3,√2.

problems.title: Equilateral cone section from a spatial height
problems.question: A section through a cone’s apex is equilateral and makes 30° with the base. The cone height is 3√3. Find the section area.
problems.idea: The section triangle’s altitude has vertical component equal to the cone height.
formulas: Triangle altitude H=cone height/sin30°; equilateral side=2H/√3.
steps: H=6√3, so the section side is 12.

problems.title: Two areas in a right triangle
problems.question: O is a cone’s base centre, B its apex, A a base-circle point, and OD⊥AB. Given areas OBD=4,OAD=1, find the base area.
problems.idea: The altitude to a hypotenuse gives a ratio of squared legs.
steps: The full right triangle OAB has area 4+1=5, which also equals (2r)r/2=r².
Hence r²=5 and the cone base area is 5π.
